segments.text: but storm clouds turn almost black.
Yet both are made of clear, colorless droplets.
Each droplet scatters every color of light equally.
That's why clouds normally look white.
Storm clouds just pack in far more droplets,
and the whole cloud is much thicker.
So light keeps hitting droplet after droplet on its way down,
and a lot of it gets scattered back upward.
That leaves much less light reaching the bottom,
so the underside of a storm cloud looks dark.
The droplets aren't different - it's just thicker and denser.
